In brief: The upcoming week in Abuja will be characterized by a prolonged period of wet weather, with rain chances remaining high throughout the 7-day forecast period, fueled by a persistent low-pressure system situated over the region. ### Monday A low-pressure system currently situated over the northwest part of the country will continue to dominate the weather pattern over Abuja, leading to a high chance of rainfall throughout the day. The temperature will rise to a high of 28°C, but the feels-like temperature will be higher, around 30°C, due to the high humidity levels. Residents in low-lying areas, such as those near the Gwarinpa district, should be prepared for potential flooding, as the rainfall accumulation is expected to range from 20-30 mm. The wind direction will be from the southwest, blowing at a moderate speed of 10 km/h, which will help to distribute the heat more evenly across the city.
The humidity levels will remain high, ranging from 80-90%, throughout the day, making the atmosphere feel very muggy and uncomfortable. As the day progresses, the rain will become more intense, with the heaviest downpours expected during the late afternoon and early evening hours. Residents in areas such as Maitama and Wuse should expect significant traffic disruptions, especially on the airport road, due to the heavy rainfall. The low-pressure system will continue to strengthen, leading to an increase in the amount of moisture being funneled into the region, which will, in turn, fuel the development of more intense thunderstorms. My best guess is that the storms will begin to dissipate by around 10 pm, but there's a chance that some light rain showers could persist into the early hours of Tuesday. The city's temperature will drop to a low of 22°C overnight, providing some relief from the heat, but the humidity will remain high, making it feel more like 25°C. The wind direction will shift to the northwest, blowing at a light speed of 5 km/h, which will help to clear out some of the moisture in the atmosphere.
